subject.title: fix(memory): keep implicit embeddings recall available

question: Should an unset or legacy-auto OpenAI embedding provider without API-key auth continue serving read-only lexical FTS recall from a valid existing index, while explicitly configured remote providers remain fail-closed?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and degraded-mode policy change, not a mechanical correctness choice; tests and runtime proof establish the implementation but cannot choose the long-term user contract.

options.title: Accept implicit FTS degradation
options.body: Merge the documented behavior so implicit/auto configuration preserves lexical recall while embeddings are unavailable and explicit remote configuration stays strict.

options.title: Preserve unavailable-search behavior
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior for implicit OpenAI embeddings and reject the fallback contract despite the proposed recovery logic.

recommendation.title: Accept implicit FTS degradation
recommendation.body: Merge the documented behavior so implicit/auto configuration preserves lexical recall while embeddings are unavailable and explicit remote configuration stays strict.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent memory runtime and OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint history makes this the best available routing candidate, though direct current-line ownership could not be verified in the read-only environment.
